records.name: The Energy Co-op
records.summary: A community energy supplier for homes and businesses in Southeastern Pennsylvania that sells wind and solar electricity. Customers who join can vote for the board and help shape its programs.
records.what_you_do: Switch your home or business power to the co-op, vote in member decisions, and attend member meetings, fairs, expos, and talks.

schedule.text: Member happy hours, fairs, expos, and talks are posted on the co-op's events page, with dates set one event at a time.

cost.text: No enrollment, membership, or cancellation fees for residential members, according to the co-op's FAQ. Your utility may still charge its own customer and delivery fees.

first_step.how: Enroll online, by email, or by phone at 215-413-2122 on a weekday. Enrolling makes you a member of the co-op.
first_step.basis: Any home or business in the service area can sign up through several clear routes, with no fees, so the way in is clear. The site describes no welcome or orientation beyond the enrollment steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: Joining means switching your electricity supplier, which usually takes 3 to 5 days. Home members pay no enrollment, membership, or cancellation fee, though your utility may still charge its own fees. You can leave at any time by telling the co-op or your utility.
first_visit_tips: If you are moving, confirm your start date with your utility before you enroll.
Customers on PECO's Customer Assistance Program cannot choose a third-party supplier, so check that first.
If you would rather talk to someone, the office is open weekdays 9 am to 5 pm.

records.notes: The FAQ does not say whether members vote or mention an annual member meeting, so the voting wording is carried over from tier 1 and is not confirmed on the FAQ. The dated items from the events page (an October 2026 overview and a June 2026 annual meeting) were left out of schedule.text as one time events. The site has no volunteer page and no accessibility statement beyond a text-size and contrast toolbar, so no access fields are recorded.

records.name: The Food Trust: Farmers Market Volunteers
records.summary: The Food Trust runs farmers markets in Philadelphia. Volunteers help at a market each week or in the office supporting one of its programs.
records.what_you_do: Help at a farmers market each week, or help in the office with a program. The group takes separate interest forms for individuals and for groups.

schedule.text: Volunteers help at a farmers market each week, or in the program office. Shift lengths and hours are not published.

locations.label: Program office
locations.address: One Penn Center, Suite 900, 1617 John F. Kennedy Blvd

cost.text: The page does not state a cost for volunteering.

first_step.how: Fill out the individual volunteer interest form on The Food Trust's site. Groups use the separate interest form for groups.
first_step.basis: The only way in that the site names is an interest form. The page does not say what happens after you submit it or describe a first shift, so a newcomer cannot see what the work is like before applying.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers help at a farmers market each week or support a program from the office. The site does not say how long a shift runs, whether there is training, or what a first day looks like. Expect to fill in the interest form first.
first_visit_tips: Fill out the individual interest form before you plan a visit, since it is the only route the site describes.
Call 215-575-0444 to ask what happens after you submit the form, because the site does not say.
Groups should use the separate interest form for groups.

records.notes: The site's /volunteer address returned a 404, so the careers page and get-involved page were used instead. Both say the same thing: an individual interest form and a separate group form, with weekly help at a market or in an office program. No shift length, training, minimum age, or first-day description is published, and the record says so rather than guessing. The newcomer rating moved from 3 to 2 because the form is the only route named and what follows it is not described. Office address is from the site's homepage.

records.name: The Friends of Mario Lanza Park
records.summary: Volunteers, formed in 1987, who look after this small historic park in Queen Village. They run regular cleanups and planting days, plus summer events: KidFest in June, Movie Nights in July, and Music Month in September.
records.what_you_do: Join a cleanup or planting day, or help with the summer events. The group asks people to email it to learn how to get involved.

schedule.text: Regular cleanups and planting days, plus a yearly run of summer events: KidFest in June, Movie Nights in July, and Music Month in September. The group's pages give no fixed day or time for work sessions.

cost.text: The group's pages list no cost for volunteering or for the summer events.

first_step.how: Email friends-mariolanzapark@qvna.org and ask about the next cleanup or planting day.
first_step.basis: The group's page invites anyone to email about volunteering, so the way in is clear. The QVNA volunteer page says most activities have flexible timing, but no beginner session or regular work-day time is listed, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a hands-on cleanup or planting in the park, done by volunteers. The pages do not say how long a session runs or what to bring. Email first to confirm the date and to ask those questions.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before you come, since no regular work-day times are posted.
Ask the group what to bring, because the pages list no tools or clothing.

records.notes: The events page lists dated Movie Nights and KidFest events for June and July 2026 at this park, so the last sign of life is July 2026. No Music Month dates appeared on the page. The QVNA volunteer page lists this and other Friends groups as links only. No work-day times, what to bring, session length, or accessibility details are published. The volunteer page also names the Weccacoe Playground and Beck Park Friends groups, listed in leads_only.

records.name: The Friends of Sedgley Woods
records.summary: Volunteers who look after Sedgley Woods, a 27-hole disc golf course in Fairmount Park. They run monthly workdays, weekly rounds, and monthly singles tournaments, and playing the course is always free.
records.what_you_do: Help with course upkeep at the second Saturday workday, or play the weekly rounds and the monthly singles tournaments.

schedule.text: Workdays on the second Saturday of each month, 9 am to noon, with tag results at 1 pm. Weekly tags on Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays all year: Saturday and Sunday start at 11 am, and Thursday start times are set by sunset. Monthly pro/am singles tournaments. The course is open from sunup to sundown.

cost.text: Playing the course is always free. The monthly singles events are described as low cost, and the site does not give an entry fee.

first_step.how: Come to the second Saturday workday, 9 am to noon, at the course, or email friendsofsedgleywoods@gmail.com to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: The About page says someone from the club will be there to answer questions and show you around, and the workdays page invites anyone to pitch in. The tags and monthly events are described as casual.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workday is a few hours of outdoor work: mowing, weed-whacking, picking up sticks and trash, and course projects. Weekend tags start at 11 am, so arrive early to check in. Discs are usually sold at the course on Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, and play is free.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's calendar or its Facebook events page before a workday, since workdays are sometimes moved or canceled.
For a weekend tag, arrive early to check in.
Ask a club member on site where to start, since the About page says someone from the club will be there to answer questions.

records.notes: The site's /faq address returned a 404, and the site has no beginner, membership, rules, or directions page, so newcomer detail comes from the About and Workdays pages. The contact page gives an email and a mailing address but no phone, transit, or parking details, so none are recorded. The events page links a 2026 events calendar but shows no month, so the 2026-10 last sign of life carried over from tier 1 is not confirmed on this pass and should be checked against that calendar. Whether discs are sold at the course and whether the tags and monthly events are casual were carried over from tier 1 and were not re-read this pass.

records.name: The German Society of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A heritage society founded in 1764 to help German immigrants. It now runs German classes, a public library, and monthly conversation evenings, film nights and book clubs for anyone who wants to learn German or enjoy German culture.
records.what_you_do: Take a German class, join the monthly conversation evening or a film night, or join a book club. Members get library borrowing and invitations to special events.

schedule.text: The monthly Konversationsabend, a German conversation evening, is on the second Wednesday from 6 to 8 pm, February to May and September to December. Friday film nights start at 6:30 pm during the film season. German classes run in terms of about 8 to 12 weeks. Yearly events include the Stiftungsfest gala, a Christkindlmarkt, and St. Martin's Parade.

cost.text: Regular 10-week classes cost $360, and the 8-week online classes cost $180 to $240. Textbooks cost about $30 to $70 extra, and private tutoring is $45 an hour. Membership dues start at $30 for students and $60 for individuals, according to the membership page, which does not say which year these apply to. The page does not list a price for the conversation evening.

access.notes: The main entry is through the parking lot door on the east side. An elevator entrance is on the Spring Garden Street side, so call 215-627-2332 during business hours so staff can unlock the gate. The Society's directions page names the Frankford Elevated ('the El') at its Spring Garden Street stop as the nearest transit, and says to walk about five blocks west from there to 7th Street.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list, then come to the second-Wednesday Konversationsabend from 6 to 8 pm.
first_step.basis: The conversation evening page says newcomers from any background are welcome, from beginner to advanced speakers, and explains how to sign up. The class page offers beginner to advanced courses, with a free level change in the first three weeks.
first_step.what_to_expect: About 20 people meet around a set theme. A speaker gives a short talk, then the group talks it over, with refreshments. The page does not list a price for the conversation evening, and classes are paid per term.
first_visit_tips: Park only in the Society's own lot behind the black gate, not under the mural, since cars there risk being towed.
Enter through the parking lot door on the east side. For the elevator entrance on Spring Garden Street, call 215-627-2332 during business hours so staff can unlock the gate.
Sign up for the mailing list first, since that is how the group announces the evening.
The Society's offices are open weekdays 9 am to 5 pm, and the Horner Memorial Library is open Tuesday and Thursday 10 am to 4 pm.

records.notes: The /library address returned a 404; the working library page is /horner-library. It says only members can borrow from the Lending Library, visitors can stop in for a tour during library hours, and research needs a request to the librarian. The page also mentions a weekly Transcription Group that is at capacity and a general volunteer form, neither recorded as a first step. The building's accessibility is not stated, so no wheelchair value is recorded. The earlier record put the El stop about five blocks east of the building; the directions page says to walk about five blocks west from that stop to 7th Street, so the record now follows the page's wording. Library hours on the library page and the directions page agree.

records.name: The Head & The Hand
records.summary: A nonprofit independent publisher and community bookstore on Frankford Avenue. It runs a writing group, a poetry book club, author events and readings, and it lets community groups book its lower-level workshop for free.
records.what_you_do: Join the writing group or the Poetry is for Everyone book club, go to an author event or reading, donate books for store credit, or book the workshop for a community meeting.

schedule.text: A writing group about once a month on a Saturday or Sunday afternoon, 2 to 3:30 pm. The Poetry is for Everyone book club meets monthly on Sunday afternoons, 2 to 3 pm. Both meet at Valerio Coffee Roasters. The store also hosts author events and a children's story time.

locations.label: Valerio Coffee Roasters, where the writing group and book club meet

cost.text: The events page gives no price for the writing group or the book club. Registration is required for the writing group. Author events vary: some are free or pay what you can, and others are ticketed.

access.notes: The lower-level community workshop is reached by a stairwell, according to the group's booking page.

first_step.how: Register on the events page for the next writing group session or Poetry is for Everyone book club meeting, then go to the venue named on that listing.
first_step.basis: The writing group is open to writers in any genre and at any stage, and the events page says to register for each session. It does not allow drop-ins, so the way in is registration. The events page does not say who can join the book club.
first_step.what_to_expect: The writing group meets for about 90 minutes with writers at any stage. The poetry book club meets for an hour, and members read and discuss one book at each meeting. Prices are not listed for these meetings, and registration is required for the writing group.
first_visit_tips: Register on the event page before you go, since the writing group does not take drop-ins.
Call 267-702-6744 or email info@theheadandthehand.com for directions, parking or transit, since the site gives none. The contact page also lists (267) 465-1784.
Check the events page for changes, since meetings are sometimes rescheduled.

records.notes: The events page says registration is required for the writing group and does not say whether the book club needs it, so the earlier wording that both required registration was corrected. The book club's June 2026 meeting is marked rescheduled with the new date still to be set; that one-time change is not written into the record. The site lists two phone numbers, (267) 465-1784 and 267-702-6744; the footer number is kept as the main contact. The site gives no parking, transit, or accessibility details beyond the stairwell note for the lower-level workshop.

records.name: The Historical Society of Frankford
records.summary: A volunteer-run history group, founded in 1905, that keeps and shares the history of Frankford. It holds monthly lectures, runs a museum open by appointment, and offers library research help.
records.what_you_do: Attend a free lecture at the Society's building, book a museum visit or research help, or watch past lectures on the Society's YouTube channel.

schedule.text: Monthly evening lectures from March to June and from September to December. Doors open at 7 pm and the talk starts at 7:30 pm. The lectures are also streamed live on the Society's Facebook page. The museum is open by appointment.

cost.text: Lectures are free and open to the public. Museum visits are by appointment, and the site lists no admission fee.

access.notes: Lectures are streamed live on the Society's Facebook page for people who cannot attend in person.

first_step.how: Come to a free monthly lecture at 1507 Orthodox Street. Doors open at 7 pm and the talk starts at 7:30 pm.
first_step.basis: Lectures are free, open to the public, and posted with a set time and place. The site does not describe any newcomer welcome beyond that, so the rating is 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: A lecture is a single evening talk in the Society's building, with doors at 7 pm and the talk at 7:30 pm. The Society says light refreshments are served. You can also watch a lecture live online.
first_visit_tips: Park in the free lot across Orthodox Street at Frankford Friends School.
Arrive when doors open at 7 pm, so you are settled before the 7:30 pm talk.
Call 215-743-6030 to ask about the next lecture or to book a museum visit, since the museum is open by appointment only.

records.notes: The museum page gives the address, phone and a contact form but does not describe how to book, admission, building access, stairs, or parking, so none of those are added beyond what the homepage says. The homepage lists the next lecture as October 13, 2026. The earlier record's mention of masks being optional at the October lecture is dropped because the current pages do not state it.
